title: the WSG holding one breath
audit_label: R454 WSG holding breath pin audit
audit_comment: The holding one breath slice pins the surfacing rate (2 inches, doubled unencumbered, needing active work - the inert body rising by natural buoyancy at one-half inch, 5 feet per round), the non-cumulative diving-bonus note (the extra depth added after encumbrance, per the 6-inch moderately-encumbered 15-foot example), the breath formula (one-third of constitution in rounds, rounded up, assuming a deep breath and no strenuous activity), the halved penalties for being unprepared or fighting (cumulative to one-fourth, with the one-round floor), the expiration rules (a Constitution Check once per round, cumulative +2 after the first, per the con-12/4-round example), the out-of-air unconsciousness with the pulled-to-surface requirement, the not-underwater one-round addition with the penalties applied after, and the hold-before-affected gas rules (rules/wsgbreath.h, prefix whb); census 378 -> 379.

banner.title: The WSG HOLDING ONE'S BREATH, R454: first the surfacing rules that open the page - the base surfacing rate, like the diving rate, is 2 inches (doubled for a character who is NOT encumbered, reduced for moderate or heavy encumbrance), and to travel upward at that rate the swimmer must be ACTIVELY working to get himself to the surface; otherwise the natural buoyancy of his body brings him to the surface at ONE-HALF inch, or 5 feet per round (modified for encumbrance), if he is inert - and it is possible to purposely encumber oneself with easily-dropped items to dive deep and return quickly after divesting the weight. The diving bonuses for leaping into the water are NOT cumulative with the depth increases for encumbered characters; the extra depth is added AFTER encumbrance is taken into account - the printed example: a moderately encumbered character diving from 15 feet travels 6 inches down, 4 for the doubled normal rate plus 2 for the leap. The breath formula: the base time a character can hold his breath underwater is a number of rounds equal to ONE-THIRD of his constitution score (ROUNDED UP), assuming a deep breath before submerging and no strenuous activity; normal movement is allowed, as are opening a locked chest, searching for a secret passage, or casting a spell. Without a chance to fill his lungs, the time is CUT IN HALF (rounded up); strenuous activity such as combat also cuts it in half; the penalties are CUMULATIVE, so an abruptly dumped character forced to fight holds his breath only ONE-FOURTH as long - but any character can hold his breath for AT LEAST ONE ROUND regardless of the penalties. When the time expires he does not automatically die: he stays alive as long as he makes a successful Constitution Check once per round, each check after the first with a CUMULATIVE +2 modifier - the printed example: a constitution of 12 holds breath for 4 rounds, the first check at the end of the 5th round unmodified, +2 at the end of the 6th, +4 at the 7th. A character who has not run out of air can surface by swimming (if proficient) or by staying still and letting buoyancy carry him up - the ONLY way a non-swimmer can surface - and can divest extra weight; a character out of air is UNCONSCIOUS, cannot move, and must be pulled to the surface before he fails a Constitution Check. Not underwater: the same formula, but ONE ROUND IS ADDED to the time limit, and the unprepared/strenuous penalties are applied AFTER that round is added, not before. And a character cannot escape a poisonous gas or noxious substance (such as the odor of a troglodyte) unless he holds his breath BEFORE he is affected - a small amount of gas is just as harmful as an extended dose. Census 378 -> 379.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed p. 43; the user own copy OCR (page 44) cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0043) - the section reads CLEAN two-way, every number (the 2-inch surfacing rate, the half-inch/5-foot inert buoyancy, the 6-inch non-cumulative example, the one-third constitution formula, the halved penalties and their one-fourth combination, the one-round floor, the cumulative +2 checks, the con-12/4-round example with the 5th/6th/7th-round check cadence, the one-round not-underwater addition and the gas rules) matched exactly; the djvu garbles only the one-third fraction glyph itself, corroborated by the printed con-12 -> 4-round example arithmetic - no eye-reads needed.
banner.sentinel: Surface at 2 inches if you work for it - drift up at half an inch, 5 feet, if you do not - and never let the leap bonus ride the encumbrance increase. A third of your constitution in rounds of air, rounded up; no deep breath or a fight halves it, both quarter it, one round is yours regardless. Past the limit, roll Constitution every round at +2 a check, until the air runs out of you and someone must pull you up. Ashore, one round more - and hold your breath before the gas, not after.

consts.name: whbBaseSurfRateIn
consts.comment: The base surfacing rate, like the diving rate, is 2 inches, doubled for a character who is not encumbered and reduced for a character who is moderately or heavily encumbered.

consts.name: whbInertRiseNum
consts.comment: The natural buoyancy of a character's body will bring him to the surface at one-half inch per round if he is inert.

consts.name: whbInertRiseDen
consts.comment: The inert rise rate is one-half inch per round, modified for encumbrance.

consts.name: whbInertRiseFt
consts.comment: The inert buoyancy rate is 5 feet per round.

consts.name: whbBreathConDiv
consts.comment: The base amount of time a character can hold his breath underwater is a number of rounds equal to one-third of his constitution score, rounded up.

consts.name: whbPenaltyDiv
consts.comment: If the character did not have a chance to fill his lungs before going under, the time is cut in half (rounded up); strenuous activity such as combat also cuts it in half.

consts.name: whbBothPenaltyDiv
consts.comment: The penalties are cumulative with each other: a character abruptly dumped into the water and then forced to fight holds his breath only one-fourth as long.

consts.name: whbMinBreathRounds
consts.comment: Any character is able to hold his breath for at least one round, regardless of the effect of these penalties.

consts.name: whbConCheckStep
consts.comment: Each Constitution Check after the first is made with a cumulative +2 modifier to the die roll.

consts.name: whbExampleCon
consts.comment: The printed example: a character with a constitution of 12 can hold his breath underwater for 4 rounds under the most favorable circumstances.

consts.name: whbExampleRounds
consts.comment: The example limit: 4 rounds for the constitution-12 character - one-third of 12.

consts.name: whbExampleFirstCheckRound
consts.comment: After 4 rounds the example character has run out of air but can still survive: the first Constitution Check comes at the end of the 5th round, +2 at the end of the 6th, +4 at the 7th.

consts.name: whbNotUwBonusRounds
consts.comment: If a character wants to hold his breath when not underwater, the formula is used but one round is added to the time limit.

bools.name: whbSurfaceRateNeedsWork
bools.comment: To be able to travel upward at the surfacing rate, the swimmer must be actively working to get himself to the surface.

bools.name: whbInertBuoyancyRise
bools.comment: Otherwise the natural buoyancy of a character's body will bring him to the surface at one-half inch (5 feet per round), modified for encumbrance, if he is inert.

bools.name: whbDeliberateEncumbranceTrick
bools.comment: It is possible for a character to purposely encumber himself with items that can be easily gotten rid of, so that he can make a deep dive and then return quickly to the surface after divesting himself of the extra weight.

bools.name: whbLeapBonusNotCumulative
bools.comment: The diving bonuses for leaping into the water are not cumulative with the depth increases for moderately, heavily and severely encumbered characters; the extra depth is added to the dive after encumbrance is taken into account.

bools.name: whbDeepBreathAssumed
bools.comment: The base breath formula assumes the character has a chance to take a deep breath before submerging and does not perform any strenuous physical activity while underwater.

bools.name: whbNormalMovementAllowed
bools.comment: Normal movement (underwater swimming, diving or surfacing) is allowed while holding breath, as are activities such as opening a locked chest, searching for a secret passage, or casting a spell if being underwater does not prohibit the casting.

bools.name: whbUnpreparedHalved
bools.comment: If the character did not have a chance to fill his lungs with air before going under, the time he can hold his breath is cut in half, rounded up.

bools.name: whbStrenuousHalved
bools.comment: If the character engages in strenuous activity such as combat, the time is also cut in half.

bools.name: whbPenaltiesCumulative
bools.comment: The unprepared and strenuous penalties are cumulative with each other - both together leave only one-fourth of the base time.

bools.name: whbAtLeastOneRound
bools.comment: Any character is able to hold his breath for at least one round, regardless of the effect of these penalties.

bools.name: whbConCheckOncePerRound
bools.comment: When the time limit expires, the character does not automatically expire: he can stay alive as long as he makes a successful Constitution Check once per round.

bools.name: whbChecksCumulativePlusTwo
bools.comment: Each Constitution Check after the first one is made with a cumulative +2 modifier to the die roll.

bools.name: whbNonswimmerBuoyancyOnly
bools.comment: A character who has not run out of air can get to the surface by swimming (if he has proficiency) or by remaining still and allowing his body's natural buoyancy to carry him upward - the only way a non-swimmer can surface.

bools.name: whbOutOfAirUnconscious
bools.comment: When a character runs out of air, he is unconscious and cannot move under his own power; to survive, he must be pulled or otherwise moved up to the surface before he fails a Constitution Check.

bools.name: whbNotUwOneRoundAdded
bools.comment: If a character wants to hold his breath when not underwater, the formula is used but one round is added to the time limit.

bools.name: whbNotUwPenaltiesAfterBonus
bools.comment: The penalties for being unprepared and for engaging in strenuous activity are applied after the one round of time is added, not before.

bools.name: whbGasHoldBeforeAffected
bools.comment: A character cannot escape the effects of a poisonous gas or some other noxious substance (such as the odor of a troglodyte) unless he holds his breath before he is affected.

bools.name: whbSmallDoseFullHarm
bools.comment: A small amount of poisonous gas is just as harmful as an extended dose - holding one's breath after ingesting some of the vapors does no good.
